title: Universal concentration of a finite flat complex from its fibres
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $E^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $S$-modules, with $E^n=0$ for all sufficiently negative $n$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that every $E^n$ is finitely generated over $S$ and flat over $R$ (tensoring with it preserves exact sequences). For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ be its residue field, and assume $H^i(E^\bullet\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))=0$ for every $i\ne0$, where tensoring is termwise. Assume also that $H^0(E^\bullet)$ is flat over $R$. Put $Z^0=\ker(d:E^0\to E^1)$ and let $T^\bullet$ have terms $T^n=E^n$ for $n<0$, $T^0=Z^0$ and $T^n=0$ for $n>0$, with the induced differentials. For every homomorphism $R\to R'$, put $S'=S\otimes_RR'$. Both maps in the canonical truncation zigzag
$$E^\bullet\otimes_RR'\ \longleftarrow\ T^\bullet\otimes_RR'\ \longrightarrow\ (H^0(E^\bullet)\otimes_RR')[0]$$
are quasi-isomorphisms of $S'$-complexes [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. The left map is induced by inclusion and the right map by $Z^0\to H^0(E^\bullet)$. Thus this specified zigzag defines an isomorphism in $D(S')$ between the two endpoint complexes, natural in maps of such complexes and in further scalar extension. No flatness or Noetherianity of $R'$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs beginning with the cokernels Q^n; general complex form of that argument, using algebra.tex Tag 00ME, lemma-mod-injective. This is a complex-theoretic input, not the diagonal duality theorem.

proof.text: For every integer $n$ set $Q^n=E^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ and write $u_n:Q^n\to E^{n+1}$ for the map induced by $d^n$. These are finite $S$-modules: the images of any finite generating list of $E^n$ generate $Q^n$. For every $R$-module $L$, right exactness identifies $Q^n\otimes_R L$ with $\operatorname{coker}(d^{n-1}\otimes1_L)$. Consequently $H^n(E^\bullet\otimes_R L)=\ker(u_n\otimes1_L)$. For $n\ne0$, taking $L=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ shows that $u_n\otimes1_L$ is injective for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs (the cokernels Q^n and the kernel Z^0)

proof.text: Fix $n\ne0$ and $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. The fraction map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is local: the preimage of $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$. The ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian, since an ideal in it is generated by the images of generators of its contraction to $S$. The module $Q^n_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite, generated by the localized generators. The module $E^{n+1}_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat: tensor any injection of $R$-modules with $E^{n+1}$, localize the resulting injection at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$, and use the natural localization-tensor isomorphism. Flatness over $R$ is equivalent to flatness over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ for this module. Localizing the fibre injection from step 1 and using that same isomorphism gives injectivity of $Q^n_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to E^{n+1}_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Here $R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}\cong\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ by $[a/s]\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$; tensoring with this quotient is quotienting by $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, by the mutually inverse formulas $x\otimes\bar r\mapsto rx$ and $[x]\mapsto x\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs (the cokernels Q^n and the kernel Z^0)

proof.text: Apply the local injectivity criterion to $u_{n,\mathfrak q}:Q^n_{\mathfrak q}\to E^{n+1}_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$. All its hypotheses were checked in step 2. It gives injectivity and an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-flat cokernel. Thus the short exact sequence with this map remains exact after tensoring with every $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module, by the flat-quotient tensor lemma. The stalkwise criterion for universal injectivity now gives that $u_n$ is $R$-universally injective. This holds independently for every $n\ne0$; no induction across degree zero is used.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs (the cokernels Q^n and the kernel Z^0)

proof.text: For every $R$-module $L$, step 1 and universal injectivity give $H^n(E^\bullet\otimes_RL)=0$ for $n\ne0$. In particular $u_1:Q^1\to E^2$ is a universally injective map into a flat module. Its cokernel sequence is universally exact (right exactness supplies the last two terms), so the flat-submodule lemma gives that $Q^1$ is $R$-flat. Let $B^1=\operatorname{im}(E^0\to E^1)$. The exact sequence $0\to B^1\to E^1\to Q^1\to0$ and the flat-kernel lemma show that $B^1$ is $R$-flat.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs (the cokernels Q^n and the kernel Z^0)

proof.text: For any $R$-module $L$, tensor the two short exact sequences $0\to Z^0\to E^0\to B^1\to0$ and $0\to B^1\to E^1\to Q^1\to0$. Their last terms are flat by step 4, so both remain short exact. The differential $E^0\otimes_RL\to E^1\otimes_RL$ factors as the resulting surjection to $B^1\otimes_RL$ followed by the resulting injection. Its kernel is therefore exactly the embedded copy of $Z^0\otimes_RL$. This identifies the specified inclusion of $T^\bullet\otimes_RL$ into $E^\bullet\otimes_RL$ with the good truncation in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs (the cokernels Q^n and the kernel Z^0)

proof.text: Write $B^0=\operatorname{im}d^{-1}\subset Z^0$ and $H=H^0(E^\bullet)=Z^0/B^0$. The sequence $0\to B^0\to Z^0\to H\to0$ stays short exact after tensoring with $L$, using the assumed flatness of $H$. The surjection $E^{-1}\to B^0$ stays surjective by right exactness. Hence the quotient map induces $H^0(T^\bullet\otimes_RL)\cong H\otimes_RL$. The inclusion into $E^\bullet\otimes_RL$ induces this same isomorphism, by step 5. In negative degrees the two complexes have identical cohomology: in degree $-1$ this follows because $Z^0\otimes_RL\to E^0\otimes_RL$ is injective, and in lower degrees their three terms and maps agree. These groups vanish by step 4; positive cohomology of $T^\bullet\otimes_RL$ is zero. Thus both specified maps induce isomorphisms in every degree. Taking $L=R\prime$ proves the asserted quasi-isomorphisms of $S\otimes_RR\prime$-complexes.

source.place: Tag 0E2F, lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing, final two paragraphs (the cokernels Q^n and the kernel Z^0)

proof.text: A chain map $f:E^\bullet\to F^\bullet$ carries $Z_E^0$ into $Z_F^0$ and $B_E^0$ into $B_F^0$, because $d_Ff=fd_E$. It therefore induces maps of the truncations and their degree-zero quotients; both zigzag squares commute already on elements, by $f(z)\mapsto[f(z)]$ and the inclusions $z\mapsto z$. Tensoring preserves these identities. For $R\to R\prime\to R\prime\prime$, the scalar comparison $(M\otimes_RR\prime)\otimes_{R\prime}R\prime\prime\cong M\otimes_RR\prime\prime$ sends $(m\otimes r\prime)\otimes r\prime\prime$ to $m\otimes r\prime r\prime\prime$, with inverse $m\otimes t\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes t$. The tensor relations verify these are inverse maps commuting with every differential, inclusion, and quotient in this zigzag. For three extensions both associations send a pure tensor to the tensor of the product of its scalar factors. Thus the comparison is compatible with further extension. Localization to the derived category inverts the left and right quasi-isomorphisms; the endpoint isomorphism is $Q(b)Q(a)^{-1}$ for the displayed arrows $a:T\otimes_RR\prime\to E\otimes_RR\prime$ and $b:T\otimes_RR\prime\to(H\otimes_RR\prime)[0]$. The commuting squares prove its naturality. None of these steps uses flatness or Noetherianity of $R\prime$.
